Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.videoconference

Class P2pSideChannel

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.videoconference.P2pSideChannel
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable, P2pNode.Listener
public final class P2pSideChannel extends Object implements P2pNode.Listener, AutoCloseable
The Video Conference app's encrypted peer-to-peer side-channel: a thin controller over the shared apps.p2p transport (P2pNode + LanDiscovery + IdentityStore) that carries meeting signaling, chat and file transfer between peers.

Boundary (by design): the real audio/video session still runs through Jitsi Meet in the system browser via JitsiUrlBuilder — this class never touches a webcam, a codec or the media path. It exists so peers can find each other on the LAN, exchange an encrypted meeting invite (a share URL), chat and swap files without a server.

Headless-safe: construction is inert. No socket is bound and no thread is started until start(String, int) is called, so the panel that owns this can be built in the headless test JVM. Every P2pSideChannel.Listener callback fires on the node's I/O thread; the UI marshals onto the EDT.

      public P2pSideChannel(IdentityStore identityStore, Path downloadDir, P2pSideChannel.Listener listener)
      Creates an inert side-channel. Nothing is bound or started until start(String, int).
      Parameters:

      downloadDir - where received files land (null falls back to a temp dir)
      listener - the event sink (may be null)

    • start

      public boolean start(String nickname, int listenPort)
      Loads (or creates) our identity, starts listening and, optionally, begins LAN discovery. Idempotent: a running channel is left untouched. Never throws; a failure is reported to the listener and false returned.
      Parameters:
      nickname - our display name (blank falls back to a fingerprint tag)
      listenPort - the TCP port to bind (<= 0 for an ephemeral port)
      Returns:
      true if the channel is now running
